title: Calcutta High Court seeks reports on 'donor quota' MBBS seats at state medical colleges
dek: A medical aspirant says donor-quota seats were filled offline outside merit counselling. The court asked the National Medical Commission and the state counselling committee to explain, and to list the ranks of those admitted.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The Calcutta High Court has directed the National Medical Commission (NMC) and the West Bengal Medical Counselling Committee (WBMCC) to file separate reports on how undergraduate medical seats under a "donor quota" at state-run colleges are being filled, after a medical aspirant who was denied an MBBS seat alleged that merit was bypassed.

Justice Amrita Sinha also asked the WBMCC to disclose the rank and marks of every candidate admitted under the quota, according to reports. The case is listed again on 4 December.

The petitioner says the seats were allotted offline, on the recommendation of private trusts, outside the online merit-based counselling that governs other seats, in breach of Supreme Court directions and NMC rules. According to reports, there are nine such undergraduate seats in Bengal's government medical colleges, and documents placed before the court show guidelines from the state Health Department and the WBMCC reserving seats at Calcutta Medical College, R.G. Kar Medical College and Calcutta National Medical College for nominees of named donors and trusts.

The quota was created to recognise families and bodies that gave land, property or money to set up or expand the institutions before they were taken over by the state, reports said. The state government has not publicly responded to the allegations.
